$comment: Fixtures for the diary→trigger inference engine (docs/trigger-model.md). Exposures are the per-pollutant scalar feature x_p in µg/m³. Predictions are [floor, ceiling] on the 1–4 Breathing Index. Priors are disabled in all cases except cold-start so expectations isolate diary-driven inference.

cases.name: cold-start: priors only, ceiling never floor
co-elevation is ambiguous: both candidates suspected
full combo repeat is guaranteed without attribution
exoneration path: clean high-ozone day attributes old entry to pm25
confirmation does not exonerate the other candidate
tolerance cascades upward: a level-2 day bounds levels 3 and 4
cases.$comment: With priors disabled, personal evidence only alarms at >= observed bad-day exposures; in production, priors cover the untested gap below.

cases.name: conflict: later tolerance beats earlier confirmation (recency wins)
confounded entries yield no constraints
severity cascades downward: a level-4 day is evidence at levels 2 and 3
U-shaped temperature via one-sided encoding: cold-dry day attributes cleanly
cases.$comment: Inference only ever sees monotone features; heat_stress and cold_dry_stress are separate dimensions, so a cold trigger says nothing about hot days.

cases.name: empty candidate set flags an unmodeled trigger, forces nothing
cases.$comment: Every modeled variable was already proven tolerable at level 3, so the bad day is unexplainable: flag as probable missing variable (pollen? indoor air?), extract no constraints.

cases.name: personal tolerance overrides priors
cases.$comment: User rated 2 at o3 168, personally refuting the population prior 'potentially 3 at 160'. The level-2 prior still applies where no tolerance evidence exists.

cases.name: pm25+humidity without observations stays ambiguous
worse-outdoors observation excludes indoor proxies from candidates
cases.$comment: Same day, but the user noticed symptoms were tied to being outside — humidity (the indoor-mold proxy) is ruled out, collapsing the candidate set to pm25 alone.

cases.name: worse-outdoors with only indoor proxies elevated flags an unmodeled outdoor trigger
cases.$comment: Symptoms tied to outside, but no modeled outdoor variable is elevated — likely an unmodeled outdoor trigger such as pollen.

cases.name: calendar pollen suspects a season and can never confirm it
cases.$comment: Hamden in August: the ragweed figure is a calendar estimate for the region, not a reading, so it is the entry's only candidate but must not become a confirmed bound — an estimate may raise a ceiling, never guarantee a floor. Repeating the exact day predicts [1,3], not [3,3].

cases.name: measured pollen confirms where the calendar could not
cases.$comment: The same day in Amsterdam, where CAMS actually measures the species. Identical vector, no estimated tag: the singleton candidate confirms and the repeat day is a floor. This is the pair that makes the rule above about provenance rather than about pollen.

cases.name: an estimate cannot carry a co-elevated day into a floor either
cases.$comment: Ozone and a calendar ragweed month together. The combination repeats, but half of it was guessed, so it stays a ceiling: the combo-repeat floor clause skips estimated constraints.

cases.name: a good day exonerates the calendar estimate that day carried
cases.$comment: Tolerance is not restricted to measured variables: rating the peak of the season easy has to be able to quiet it, or a calendar suspicion would alarm every August forever.

cases.name: correlated variables (heat+ozone) stay ambiguous but the combo predicts
